subject: Genetics
title: Genomic Privacy
description: A fast breakdown of Genomic Privacy for builders.

hook.text: Your genome is the most personal data possible. It identifies you, your family, your disease risks. It can't be changed.

buildup.text: GINA, passed in 2008, bans genetic discrimination in employment and health insurance.

discovery.text: Researchers re-identified 'anonymous' genome donors using public genealogy databases. Anonymity was an illusion.

twist.text: If one relative shares their DNA, yours is partially exposed. You didn't consent. A cousin decided for you.

climax.text: Genomic data breaches can't be fixed. You can change a password. You can't change your genome. The stakes are permanent.

punchline.text: Your genome is the one password you can never reset.

quiz.question: What does the GINA law protect against?
options: Genetic discrimination in employment and health insurance
